name: Jian tenmoku ware
summary: Dark stoneware tea bowls of the Song dynasty. A thick iron-rich glaze runs down the cone-shaped bowl in streaks and spots and pools in a bead at the foot.

philosophy.core_thesis: A bowl for whisked white tea must be dark, so that the foam shows; the kiln, not the brush, makes the pattern in an iron-rich glaze.
design_principles: Make the bowl dark, because the white foam of whisked tea must show against it.
Throw a cone with a thick wall, 6 to 9 mm, to keep the tea hot.
Pull in the rim below the lip, so that the tea does not spill and the foam stays in the bowl.
Dip the bowl in an iron glaze that holds 5 to 9 per cent iron oxide.
Let the glaze run: stop it about 1 cm above the foot, where it ends in a thick bead.
Fire in reduction to about 1300 °C so that the iron forms streaks, drops and spots.
Leave the foot ring and the lower wall bare, in a dark grey or purple-brown clay.
Add a silver or copper band on the rim for a bowl of high rank.
anti_patterns: A bright, clean white or cream body shown over the whole bowl
A painted or printed pattern on the glaze
A flat even glaze with no streaks, spots or bead at the foot
A thin porcelain wall that burns the hand when the tea is hot

form.shape: A deep conical tea bowl with a wide mouth, made for whisked powdered tea. A small number of ewers and stands accompany it in the tea service.
form.profile: Straight sides rise at about 45 degrees from a small foot and turn in just below the lip, so that the rim shows a clear step.
form.foot_and_rim: A short, narrow, bare foot with a straight-cut ring; the rim is thin where the glaze breaks to brown and the lip may carry a silver band.
form.proportion: Diameter 11 to 13 cm and height 6 to 7 cm; the wall is 6 to 9 mm thick and the bowl feels heavy for its size.
rules: Keep the cone shape and the step below the lip.
Keep the foot small and bare, and the lower wall unglazed.
Choose a body that fires dark grey, brown or purple-black, rich in iron.
Make the bowl fit one hand and hold hot tea without a handle.

bodies.rule: Use a local stoneware clay that is rich in iron and fires to dark grey or brown. Keep a white body out: the dark clay adds colour to the glaze.

methods: throwing on the wheel in one cone
turning the foot ring when leather-hard
dipping the bowl in glaze by hand, with the foot held in the fingers
stacking the bowls in saggars, one in each
forming.joins: The bowl has no joins; a metal rim band of silver or copper is fixed on the lip after the firing.
forming.details: A bead of glaze at the foot, thin brown breaks at the rim, finger marks where the potter held the bowl, and sand marks under the foot from the saggar.

glaze.pattern: Fine streaks like a hare's fur, round silver spots like oil on water, or feather marks like a partridge; the kiln makes each one.
glaze.gloss: Glossy to high gloss, about 70 to 95 GU on the glazed wall; the bare foot is dull.
glaze.wear: The rim wears to a brown line where the glaze is thin. The silver band tarnishes, and the glaze keeps its depth.

palette.strategy: Black to brown glaze with silver, russet or blue-grey streaks and spots. The only light colour is the bare grey clay at the foot.

firing.kiln: A long climbing dragon kiln on a hill slope, fired with wood; the bowls stand in saggars in rows.
processes: single high firing of the bowl with the glaze on the raw or lightly fired clay
slow cooling, so that iron crystals grow in the glaze
hold at the peak, so that the glaze runs and forms the bead
firing.scale: Many kilns in the hills of Fujian made thousands of bowls for the market, and the court chose the best for tribute.
firing.signs: A bead of glaze at the foot, stilt or sand marks under the foot, and spots of different size where gas bubbles broke in the glaze.

pieces.form: Conical bowl with fine hare's-fur streaks that run from the rim to the foot
Bowl with silver oil spots on a black ground and a silver rim band
Bowl with partridge-feather mottling and a thick bead at the foot
Bowl with the lower wall and foot left in bare dark clay

lineage.root: Song potters in Fujian made the first dark tea bowls in this data; no earlier style here leads to it.

emotion.target_response: A deep, quiet calm. The viewer looks into a dark bowl and sees a night sky of small lights.

use_cases: a still-life prompt with a dark tea bowl
a glaze brief for iron-rich reduction glazes
a museum label for a Song tea bowl
avoid_when: the brief needs a pale or celadon bowl
the brief needs a handle or a lid

modifiers.request: hand-formed and softer, for a Japanese tea room
modifiers.how: Hand-build a rounded bowl in open clay and fire it low and hot to 900 °C with a lead glaze.

modifiers.request: steeped tea, a pot instead of a bowl
modifiers.how: Change the form to a small teapot in unglazed red stoneware that fires to about 1150 °C.

wall_thickness.note: Jian bowls are thick for the size; the wall holds the heat of the tea.
